outcome: spontaneous labor before scheduled cesarean delivery
cohort: 1221 Thai and other Southeast Asian pregnant women scheduled for either an elective repeat cesarean delivery or an elective primary cesarean delivery at 37-40 weeks of gestation
finding: While there were no significant differences in severe maternal complications between performing an elective cesarean delivery at 39 weeks and other gestational ages, severe neonatal complications were significantly decreased when a cesarean delivery was performed electively from 38 weeks onwards.
mod_finding: Scheduling a cesarean delivery at 37 or 38 weeks decreased the risk of spontaneous labor compared to 39 weeks.
